definition: Backpropagation through structure (BPTS) is a gradient-based technique for training recursive neural networks, proposed in a 1996 paper written by Christoph Goller and Andreas Küchler.
details: Backpropagation through structure (BPTS) is a gradient-based technique for training recursive neural networks, proposed in a 1996 paper written by Christoph Goller and Andreas Küchler.
story: Picture a potter shaping clay on a spinning wheel: every nudge is tiny, but each one is guided by how the last attempt wobbled. Underneath all the magic is a patient process of small improvements. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. Each pass is a tiny course-correction — the model gets a little less wrong every time. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Backpropagation through structure.
